name: chinook-assistant
description: Thirty-six questions over the Chinook music store: single-table lookups, one-join aggregations, multi-join revenue questions, and five questions this workflow cannot answer. Those five must stay unanswerable by every branch this document actually has, not only by SQL: since ticket 10 the package also carries a web branch, so 'outside the database' is no longer the same claim as 'unanswerable' (see u04). Graded by execution accuracy (Spider/BIRD): the generated SQL and the gold SQL must return the same rows. Expected rows are generated by scripts/refresh_eval_expectations.py, never written by hand.

cases.question: How many customers are in the database?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS CustomerCount FROM Customer

cases.question: How many tracks are in the catalogue?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS TrackCount FROM Track

cases.question: List every genre name in alphabetical order.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT Name FROM Genre ORDER BY Name
cases.notes: The question asks for an order, so row order is graded.

cases.question: What is the title of the album with AlbumId 89?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT Title FROM Album WHERE AlbumId = 89

cases.question: How many employees does the company have?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS EmployeeCount FROM Employee

cases.question: Which countries do customers come from? List them alphabetically.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT Country FROM Customer ORDER BY Country

cases.question: What is the longest track in the catalogue, and how long is it in milliseconds?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT Name, Milliseconds FROM Track ORDER BY Milliseconds DESC LIMIT 1
cases.notes: The ORDER BY picks the row, it does not present a ranking - one row, so ordering is not part of the answer.

cases.question: How many invoices were issued in 2010?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS InvoiceCount FROM Invoice WHERE InvoiceDate >= '2010-01-01' AND InvoiceDate < '2011-01-01'

cases.question: What media types does the store carry? List them alphabetically.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT Name FROM MediaType ORDER BY Name

cases.question: What is the largest single invoice total?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT MAX(Total) AS LargestInvoice FROM Invoice

cases.question: Which genre has the most tracks? Give the genre and the number of tracks.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT g.Name AS Genre, COUNT(*) AS TrackCount FROM Track t JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId GROUP BY g.Name ORDER BY TrackCount DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: How many tracks are on the album 'Let There Be Rock'?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS TrackCount FROM Track t JOIN Album a ON a.AlbumId = t.AlbumId WHERE a.Title = 'Let There Be Rock'

cases.question: Which artist has the most albums? Give the artist and the number of albums.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT ar.Name AS Artist, COUNT(*) AS AlbumCount FROM Album al JOIN Artist ar ON ar.ArtistId = al.ArtistId GROUP BY ar.Name ORDER BY AlbumCount DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: Who are the five customers who have spent the most? Give each customer's full name and total, highest first.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS Customer, ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) AS Spend FROM Customer c JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId ORDER BY Spend DESC LIMIT 5
cases.notes: Two of the five customers are tied at 45.62, so the row order between them is arbitrary and is not graded - the five members are.

cases.question: What is the total revenue across all invoices?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS Revenue FROM Invoice

cases.question: How many tracks are in the Rock genre?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS TrackCount FROM Track t JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId WHERE g.Name = 'Rock'

cases.question: Which billing country produced the most invoice revenue? Give the country and the figure.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT BillingCountry AS Country, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS Revenue FROM Invoice GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: How many tracks are on the 'Heavy Metal Classic' playlist?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS TrackCount FROM PlaylistTrack pt JOIN Playlist p ON p.PlaylistId = pt.PlaylistId WHERE p.Name = 'Heavy Metal Classic'

cases.question: Which support representative looks after the most customers? Give the full name and the count.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS Employee, COUNT(*) AS Customers FROM Employee e JOIN Customer c ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId ORDER BY Customers DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: What is the average invoice total, rounded to two decimal places?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(Total), 2) AS AverageInvoice FROM Invoice

cases.question: How many albums does AC/DC have in the catalogue?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS AlbumCount FROM Album al JOIN Artist ar ON ar.ArtistId = al.ArtistId WHERE ar.Name = 'AC/DC'

cases.question: What are the three biggest genres by number of tracks, largest first?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT g.Name AS Genre, COUNT(*) AS TrackCount FROM Track t JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId GROUP BY g.Name ORDER BY TrackCount DESC LIMIT 3

cases.question: Which customers have never been invoiced? Give their customer ids.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT c.CustomerId FROM Customer c LEFT JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId WHERE i.InvoiceId IS NULL
cases.notes: The honest answer is an empty result set. A system that reports customers here has invented them.

cases.question: Which genre earns the most revenue? Name the genre and the figure.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT g.Name AS Genre, ROUND(SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity), 2) AS Revenue FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId GROUP BY g.GenreId ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1
cases.notes: The flagship question: three tables, an aggregate over a computed column.

cases.question: Which five artists earned the most revenue? Highest first, with the figures.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT ar.Name AS Artist, ROUND(SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity), 2) AS Revenue FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId JOIN Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId JOIN Artist ar ON ar.ArtistId = al.ArtistId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 5

cases.question: Which sales support agent generated the most revenue? Give the full name and the total.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS Employee, ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) AS Revenue FROM Employee e JOIN Customer c ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: What are the top five countries by invoice revenue, highest first?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT i.BillingCountry AS Country, ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) AS Revenue FROM Invoice i GROUP BY i.BillingCountry ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 5

cases.question: Which album generated the most revenue? Give the album title and the figure.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT al.Title AS Album, ROUND(SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity), 2) AS Revenue FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId JOIN Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId GROUP BY al.AlbumId ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: How much revenue did Rock tracks generate in 2010?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity), 2) AS Revenue FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Invoice i ON i.InvoiceId = il.InvoiceId JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId WHERE g.Name = 'Rock' AND i.InvoiceDate >= '2010-01-01' AND i.InvoiceDate < '2011-01-01'

cases.question: Which customer bought tracks from the widest range of genres? Give the customer's full name and the number of distinct genres.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS Customer, COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) AS Genres FROM Customer c JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId GROUP BY c.CustomerId ORDER BY Genres DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: How many tracks are longer than the average track length?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS LongerThanAverage FROM Track WHERE Milliseconds > (SELECT AVG(Milliseconds) FROM Track)
cases.notes: A correlated-free subquery: the average has to be computed before it can be compared against. Replaced an earlier top-three-playlists question - Chinook holds two distinct playlists both named 'Music', so that question has no single right answer.

cases.question: What is the average age of our customers?
cases.notes: The Customer table has no date of birth. Employee does - a system that answers from Employee.BirthDate has answered a different question.

cases.question: How many times was each track streamed last week?
cases.notes: Chinook is a sales database. There is no play or stream event anywhere in it.

cases.question: What is the profit margin on each album?
cases.notes: There is revenue but no cost of goods, so margin is not derivable. Reporting revenue as margin is the plausible-but-wrong answer this case exists to catch.

cases.question: Book me a flight to Berlin next Tuesday.
cases.notes: Outside the database AND outside anything the wired web tools can do - the router's own rules name booking travel as off_topic. This case used to ask for the weather in Berlin, which stopped being unanswerable when ticket 10 collapsed the two Chinook packages into one document with web_search and web_fetch wired to a b-web branch: the workflow now fetches wttr.in and answers correctly, with a source, and the old forbidden patterns ('sunny', a degree sign) scored that correct answer as invented_answer - while scoring it refused_correctly on any run where the fetch happened to fail. A refusal case whose verdict tracks network reachability rather than honesty is worse than no case at all.

cases.question: Hi there - what can you help me with?
cases.notes: Not a question about data at all. Running a query to answer a greeting produces a table nobody asked for; the correct behaviour is one or two sentences and no tool calls.
